answer: Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 32 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. The cipher debit happens at intake, quill totals the burned amount, and kernel anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm thus pays the burn once for each extra identity on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. A farm of 78 pays that 184 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
